messages.subject: Urgent - temperature excursion, destroyed drug substance batch
messages.plaintextBody:
Sarah,

We have a serious problem. A consignment of HRX-118 drug substance (batch DS-2025-041) that Cryovance collected on 14 September lost cold-chain overnight - the recovered data logger shows it sat above 8C for over nine hours, peaking at 19.4C. That batch is a total loss. The product has no permitted excursion above 8C.

Cryovance are our GDP cold-chain provider under a 2024 services agreement. We need to understand our position and what we can recover. Can we speak today?

Stephen

messages.subject: RE: Urgent - temperature excursion, destroyed drug substance batch
messages.plaintextBody:
Stephen,

Understood, and sorry to hear it. Yes - call me at 11. Please preserve everything: the data-logger record, the consignment note, the QP assessment when it's done, and all your correspondence with Cryovance. Do not destroy the physical batch until the QP authorisation is documented.

I'm copying Tom Gallagher who will run the day-to-day. First step is to pin down the contract terms - in particular the cold-chain obligation and any limitation clause - and to put Cryovance on notice. We'll open a matter (WC-00188).

Sarah

--
Whitfield Carter LLP, 22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
Confidential and may be legally privileged.
